title: Egress proxies
intro.1: Let a session’s traffic leave through an upstream proxy you choose, such as a residential or ISP proxy, with the browser’s time zone and languages set to match.
add-a-proxy.title: Add a proxy
add-a-proxy.1: In the dashboard, open Proxies and add one: a name, and the proxy’s address with its credentials. easi.run checks it before it saves it, and saves it only if the check passes. The check learns the country the proxy’s traffic leaves from, and the proxy takes that country’s time zone and languages, which you can change.
add-a-proxy.5: 1–32 characters of a–z, 0–9 and -, unique. What people pick when they start a session, and what agents name.
add-a-proxy.7: http://, https:// or socks5://, then [user[:password]@]host:port. Percent-encode the user and password. With SOCKS5, a user name needs a password, neither empty. {session} in the user name becomes the session’s id (a persistent session’s own, the same at each resume), for providers that keep one exit address per user name.
add-a-proxy.9: An IANA name, such as America/Sao_Paulo. By default, the one the proxy’s country suggests.
add-a-proxy.11: 1–8 tags such as pt-BR, preferred first. By default, the proxy’s country’s, then en-US and en.
add-a-proxy.12: Up to 32 proxies. A new address for a proxy is checked the same way, and replaces the old one only if it passes.
the-check.title: The check
the-check.1: The check runs from where a session’s proxy will reach the upstream, on a network made like a session’s. Through the upstream, it reaches the DNS-over-HTTPS resolver every session through an egress uses, and fetches the metadata Cloudflare’s speed test reads (https://speed.cloudflare.com/meta, its certificate verified), which confirms the proxy works and says the address its traffic leaves from, its country and, when known, its region and city. The check itself takes at most 10 seconds, and says what went wrong when it fails: the proxy cannot be reached, it timed out, it refused the credentials or the connection, a TLS certificate did not verify, it does not speak its protocol, or the speed test answered something else.
the-check.2: A session starts through a proxy only after a check of the very upstream it will use passes, before any of the session’s containers is created; a proxy the same for every session counts a check that passed in the last 30 seconds. You can check a saved proxy again from the Proxies page at any time.
the-check.3: Proxies’ credentials are kept in the admin’s state volume (egresses.json, readable by the admin only), so a backup of that volume holds them. The dashboard never shows them again: each proxy lists its address, whether it has a user name and a password, its country, time zone and languages. Only the administrator adds, changes or removes proxies; agents start sessions through them by name.
what-goes-through-it.title: What goes through it
what-goes-through-it.1: Everything the browser loads, DNS included (over DNS-over-HTTPS through the upstream).
